messages:
maya_oncall: Alert — control-plane heartbeat p95 spike detected in us-east-1. Autoscaler started ejecting nodes at ~16:17 UTC, ~42 GPU nodes marked unhealthy. Putting timeline here for the postmortem.

monitoring-bot: [ALERT] 2026-03-12T16:17:02Z cluster/us-east-1 control-plane.heartbeat.p95=1.25s, lost-heartbeats=42

jeff_runtime: Confirming. We see a sharp cluster of missed heartbeats rather than a slow drift. Many eviction events are effectively simultaneous.

priya_sre: Repro logs: admission-controller immediately attempted full rebalancing which pushed traffic cross-region. us-west and eu-central admission queues saturated.

li_infra: Network telemetry from us-east shows an eBPF drop spike across control-plane subnets for ~45s starting 16:17:00 UTC. Suspect transient router flapping or noisy tenant flow.

maya_oncall: Noting that our conservative throttles kick in when we lose heartbeats. That policy probably amplified load instead of smoothing it.

jeff_runtime: We also rolled out a tuning change yesterday: heartbeat_grace_ms lowered from 4000 -> 1000 to speed failover. That made short network hiccups fatal.

ana_product: (ana_product) Any customer-visible metrics?

sam_support: Support saw ~60% spike in error tickets for hosted inference in the 16:18-16:40 window. Several customers retried aggressively which worsened the burst.

jeff_runtime: Log snippet around the window:
```
16:17:00.112 control-agg: nodepool-east-1 heartbeat=missed
16:17:00.113 autoscaler: mark_unhealthy node=gpuprod-e-12
16:17:00.114 router: reassign 1200 req/min -> us-west
16:17:00.158 monitoring: eBPF drop rate spike on cp-subnet-3
16:17:00.240 autoscaler: mark_unhealthy node=gpuprod-e-13
```

priya_sre: Mitigations we applied (ordered):
- 16:24 UTC: rolled heartbeat_grace_ms back to 4000
- 16:24 UTC: added regional admission throttles (temporary) to avoid full fanout
- 16:26 UTC: provisioned emergency burst tokens in us-west

li_infra: At 16:30 UTC we swapped a flaky border router and cleared the eBPF ruleset; packet drop returned to baseline.

maya_oncall: Short timeline summary:
- 16:17:00 UTC: eBPF/router blip in us-east-1
- 16:17-16:20 UTC: control-plane marks many nodes unhealthy (fast grace window)
- 16:18-16:28 UTC: traffic reassignments cause admission saturation in other regions
- 16:24 UTC: grace window rollback; 16:30 UTC infra fix; 16:40 UTC traffic stabilized

jeff_runtime: Root cause: Primary = aggressive heartbeat timeout change combined with a transient network fault. Contributing = admission controller lacks gradual ramp/failover damping, so full-scale spillover happened.

ana_product: Impact: several hosted customers saw ~5-15s increased tails and ~2% elevation in 5xx for ~22 minutes. Dedicated pools in e-region lost throughput during evacuation. We'll need to surface affected customers for CS.

priya_sre: Action items (owners):
- jeff_runtime: revert the heartbeat_grace_ms change permanently; add a canary and automated tests for heartbeat sensitivity
- li_infra: add stronger border-router monitoring + automated eBPF rollback playbook
- priya_sre: implement gradual regional spillover (token-bucket based) to avoid instant fanout
- ana_product: draft customer comms and impact notes for CS
- maya_oncall: add alert for simultaneous >10 node ejections within 30s

jeff_runtime: Additional: I'll implement a router load-shedding policy to prefer local queuing over instant cross-region failover. PR and benching scheduled.

li_infra: I'll run a post-deploy test for eBPF rule rollbacks and add a synthetic control-plane heartbeat path check.

maya_oncall: I'll convert this into a full postmortem doc with timeline and action tracker and ping owners for due dates.

sam_support: CS: I'll prioritize reaching out to customers who reported errors and attach sample request IDs/logs.

monitoring-bot: Incident resolved at 16:40:12 UTC. Alerts recovered. control-plane.heartbeat.p95 is back to ~80ms.

maya_oncall: Closing notes: do not push aggressive failure-detection defaults globally without regional canaries. Prefer safer defaults + staged rollout for any speedups to failure detection. :white_check_mark:
